stories.title: You Can't Escape AI. Here's How to Live With It.
stories.take: Molick's playbook: use the best paid model as a second opinion on medicine, taxes and finances • Build what AI can't replace — deep expertise, breadth, taste and agency • Prompt like a manager: specify the product, the quality bar and the tests, and ask for five mock-ups to pick from • Give agents guardrails: no credit cards, their own email address, and they must always identify themselves

stories.title: How America became a fearful nation that normalized white supremacy
stories.take: Reitman's answer: 9/11 collapsed 1990s optimism into a nation afraid — civil liberties traded for security, a forever war on terror, and Iraq sold on WMD claims that shifted when they collapsed • A quarter of troops came home with untreated PTSD or TBI • Marine-turned-Identity Europa founder Nathan Demigo mainstreamed 'you will not replace us' and pushed infiltration of campuses, school boards and law enforcement • The legal asymmetry: joining ISIS is material support, joining a domestic white-nationalist group is protected speech

stories.title: Why Steve Eisman Isn't Buying Anthropic's IPO
stories.take: Eisman says no: there are 'no moats around this business' and share gains appear to come only through price • $800–900B in future capital commitments sits against that price-based franchise, and the costs are not yet in the income statement • The S-1 stops at Q2 and omits Q3, when sequential growth fell from 147% to 45% after token maxing ended • A reported ~50% October price cut is unanswered, and one founder-controlled Class F share carries 50.1% of the vote

stories.title: Is Running From Trump Enough to Save Republicans on Tuesday?
stories.take: Only Susan Collins (ME) and John Sununu (NH) — their distance from Trump appears sufficient to stay competitive, with Sununu trailing by about 5 points • Ashley Hinson (IA) and Roger Marshall (KS) still rely on strong Trump ties, suggesting distancing alone won't save them

stories.title: Is it time to abolish the MBA?
stories.take: Cambridge professor Chris Marcus says yes — 'We don't need to fix business schools. We need to abolish them,' arguing they promote deal-making and shareholder capitalism while squashing students' public-good ambitions • Wharton dean Erica James says evolve, don't abolish • Case studies are biased by company sign-off and winner-heavy selection — Harvard ran multiple positive Enron cases before the fraud broke • About 80% of grads at some top schools end up in just consulting, finance or tech; median MBA ROI is about $665,000 over 10 years

stories.title: Can Netanyahu Hold On?
stories.take: No — Netanyahu's bloc holds only about 55 seats and needs 61 of 120; the opposition has roughly 49, leaving a deadlock • Turnout hit 77%, the highest since 1999, driven by strong Arab-Israeli participation • Analysts say his leverage is a unity government or the Iran threat to force coalition talks • The US and Israel are weighing post-midterm escalation options against Iran
